task1.title: Average retirement age for men and women, 2004 and 2008
task1.prompt: The graphs below show the average retirement age for men and women in 2004 and 2008 in six different countries.

chartDesc.title: Average retirement age of men / Average retirement age of women
chartDesc.overview: Overall, average retirement ages increased or stayed the same across all six countries from 2004 to 2008 for both sexes. Sweden consistently had the highest retirement age for both men and women, while France generally had among the lowest.
keyFeatures: Highest retirement age in both years was in Sweden for both men (63 in 2004, 64 in 2008) and women (63 in 2004, 64 in 2008).
Lowest retirement age for men was in France in 2004 at 58 years.
Retirement age remained unchanged for Italian men at 60 years and French women at 59 years across both 2004 and 2008.
Denmark experienced the largest increase for women, rising by 2 years from 59 in 2004 to 61 in 2008.

task1.instruction: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
task1.sampleBand8:
The two bar charts compare the average age at which men and women retired in six European countries in 2004 and 2008.

Overall, there was a clear upward trend in retirement ages over the period in almost every case, and men consistently retired later than women in most countries. Sweden sat at the top of the range for both sexes, while France was generally at the bottom.

Among men, Swedish workers retired latest, at 63 in 2004 and 64 in 2008, followed by the Netherlands, where the figure rose from 62 to 63. The most pronounced increase, however, occurred in France, where the average climbed from just 58 to 60, while Italy was the only country where the male retirement age remained unchanged, at 60. Danish and British men each worked one year longer by 2008, retiring at 61 and 62 respectively.

The pattern for women was broadly similar but at slightly lower ages. Swedish women again retired latest, at 63 rising to 64, whereas women in Denmark, France and Italy all retired at around 59 in 2004. By 2008 the Danish figure had risen by two full years to 61, the largest female increase, while France was the only country where the age stood at the same level, 59, in both years. As a result, the gender gap in retirement ages narrowed slightly in several countries by the end of the period.
task1.uzSampleBand8:
Ikkita ustunli diagramma olti Yevropa mamlakatida erkaklar va ayollarning 2004 va 2008-yillardagi o'rtacha pensiyaga chiqish yoshini solishtiradi.

Umuman olganda, davr mobaynida deyarli barcha holatlarda pensiya yoshida yaqqol o'sish tendensiyasi kuzatildi va ko'pchilik mamlakatlarda erkaklar ayollardan doimiy ravishda kechroq pensiyaga chiqdi. Har ikkala jins bo'yicha ham Shvetsiya ro'yxatning eng yuqorisida, Fransiya esa odatda eng pastida turdi.

Erkaklar orasida shvetsiyaliklar eng kech — 2004-yilda 63, 2008-yilda 64 yoshda — pensiyaga chiqdi, undan keyin ko'rsatkich 62 dan 63 ga ko'tarilgan Niderlandiya turadi. Biroq eng keskin o'sish Fransiyada yuz berdi: u yerda o'rtacha yosh atigi 58 dan 60 ga ko'tarildi, Italiya esa erkaklar pensiya yoshi 60 da o'zgarishsiz qolgan yagona mamlakat bo'ldi. Daniya va Britaniya erkaklari 2008-yilga kelib bir yildan ko'proq ishlab, mos ravishda 61 va 62 yoshda pensiyaga chiqdi.

Ayollardagi manzara ham shunga o'xshash, ammo biroz pastroq yoshlarda kuzatildi. Shvetsiyalik ayollar yana eng kech — 63 dan 64 ga ko'tarilgan yoshda — pensiyaga chiqdi, Daniya, Fransiya va Italiyadagi ayollar esa 2004-yilda taxminan 59 yoshda ishdan to'xtagan. 2008-yilga kelib Daniya ko'rsatkichi rosa ikki yilga oshib 61 ga yetdi — bu ayollar orasidagi eng katta o'sish — Fransiya esa yosh har ikkala yilda ham bir xil, 59 darajasida turgan yagona mamlakat bo'ldi. Natijada davr oxiriga kelib bir qancha mamlakatlarda pensiya yoshidagi gender farqi biroz qisqardi.

task2.title: Newspapers versus other forms of media
task2.prompt: Some people think that newspapers are the best way to learn the news. However, others believe that they can get the news more effectively through other forms of media. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
task2.instruction: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
task2.sampleBand8:
How people follow the news has changed dramatically in recent years. While some still regard newspapers as the best source, others find television, websites and social media far more effective. I largely agree with the second group, although newspapers retain some important strengths.

Supporters of newspapers argue that printed journalism offers unmatched depth and reliability. Articles are usually fact-checked before publication and held to strict editorial standards, and long-form reporting provides in-depth analysis that a thirty-second bulletin cannot. For many readers, sitting down with a paper also encourages calmer, more focused reading than endless scrolling does.

However, other forms of media clearly outperform print in several respects. Speed is the most obvious: online platforms report breaking news within minutes and update their coverage as a story unfolds, whereas a newspaper is already a day old when it is printed. Digital outlets are also more accessible — anyone with a phone has dozens of sources at their fingertips, usually free of charge — and they combine text with video, live maps and expert discussion in a way paper never can. Radio and television, meanwhile, serve people who cannot or prefer not to read.

In my opinion, modern media are, on balance, the more effective way to learn the news, simply because they are faster, richer and more portable. Nevertheless, the credibility that quality newspapers have built remains essential in an age of online misinformation, so the wisest approach is to rely on digital channels that maintain traditional journalistic standards.
task2.uzSampleBand8:
Odamlarning yangiliklarni kuzatish usuli so'nggi yillarda keskin o'zgardi. Ba'zilar hamon gazetalarni eng yaxshi manba deb bilsa, boshqalar televideniye, veb-saytlar va ijtimoiy tarmoqlarni ancha samaraliroq deb hisoblaydi. Men asosan ikkinchi guruhga qo'shilaman, garchi gazetalarning ayrim muhim afzalliklari saqlanib qolgan bo'lsa ham.

Gazeta tarafdorlari bosma jurnalistika tengsiz chuqurlik va ishonchlilik taklif etishini ta'kidlaydilar. Maqolalar odatda chop etilishidan oldin faktlari tekshiriladi va qat'iy tahririyat mezonlariga bo'ysunadi, keng ko'lamli reportajlar esa o'ttiz soniyalik xabar bera olmaydigan chuqur tahlilni taqdim etadi. Ko'plab o'quvchilar uchun gazeta bilan o'tirish cheksiz varaqlashdan ko'ra xotirjamroq va diqqatliroq mutolaani ham rag'batlantiradi.

Biroq boshqa media turlari bir necha jihatdan bosma nashrlardan aniq ustun keladi. Eng yaqqoli — tezlik: onlayn platformalar shoshilinch yangiliklarni bir necha daqiqada yetkazadi va voqea rivojlanib borgani sari yoritishni yangilab boradi, gazeta esa chop etilgan paytdayoq bir kunlik eskirgan bo'ladi. Raqamli nashrlar ham qulayroq — telefoni bor har bir kishi o'nlab manbalarni odatda bepul qo'l ostida tutadi — va ular matnni video, jonli xaritalar hamda ekspert muhokamasi bilan qog'oz hech qachon qila olmaydigan tarzda uyg'unlashtiradi. Radio va televideniye esa o'qiy olmaydigan yoki o'qishni istamaydigan odamlarga xizmat qiladi.

Mening fikrimcha, zamonaviy media umumiy hisobda yangiliklarni bilishning samaraliroq yo'lidir, chunki u tezroq, boyroq va ko'chmadir. Shunga qaramay, sifatli gazetalar shakllantirgan ishonchlilik onlayn dezinformatsiya davrida hamon muhim bo'lib qolmoqda, shuning uchun eng oqilona yo'l — an'anaviy jurnalistika mezonlarini saqlab qolgan raqamli kanallarga tayanishdir.
